declared_purpose: Send selected local files/directories through Xdrop using encrypted share links, or download and decrypt a full share link locally. The entry requires the fragment key and preservation of built-in path sanitization and transfer cleanup; verification with a small temporary file is conditional on user request. Metadata selection, progress logging and default expiry are implementation choices (SKILL.md:8-19, 21-44, 46-80).

data_operations.operation: Read local configuration and command arguments
data_operations.source: Upload/download argument parsers and process environment
data_operations.data_scope: Selected input paths, share URL, destination, display name, expiry, concurrency, output flags, XDROP_SERVER and XDROP_API_URL; no general environment collection.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory. API destination is the explicit override/environment value or the server origin's /api/v1.
data_operations.condition: When the corresponding CLI is invoked.

data_operations.operation: Enumerate selected files and derive metadata locally
data_operations.data_scope: Absolute paths, relative paths including directory root names, basenames, sizes and modification times; MIME type inferred from extension. Directory traversal recursively includes regular files without a filename exclusion filter.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local upload process memory; absolute paths are used for reads and are not fields in the constructed manifest.
data_operations.condition: Upload inputs are collected before transfer creation; directory entries that are neither files nor directories are skipped.

data_operations.operation: Select or infer a transfer display name
data_operations.data_scope: Explicit --name, or a helper-derived name based on paths and file count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local memory, then the encrypted manifest.
data_operations.condition: Normal CLI parsing defaults name to an empty string, so main's nullish fallback does not call defaultDisplayName. The exported helper can infer a name when called separately.

data_operations.operation: Create a remote transfer and disclose unencrypted control metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Requested expiry; transfer/file identifiers, file count, exact plaintext and ciphertext lengths, chunk sizes/counts/indexes and ciphertext SHA-256 checksums. Server-issued manageToken authenticates subsequent management requests.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured Xdrop API: /transfers and the transfer's /files, /upload-urls, /chunks/complete and /finalize endpoints. manageToken is sent as an Authorization bearer credential.
data_operations.condition: Creation precedes file-count/size validation; subsequent requests occur as upload progresses. These fields expose file structure and lengths despite content encryption.

data_operations.operation: Read, encrypt and upload selected file contents
data_operations.data_scope: Selected file bytes, including any embedded metadata; locally generated rootKey, file identifiers and nonces. File chunks are encrypted with AES-GCM using derived file keys; checksums cover ciphertext.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Plaintext and keys remain in local processing; ciphertext is PUT to each URL returned by the upload-URLs API. These requests contain no manageToken header in the supplied code.
data_operations.condition: After registration, for every prepared chunk, with configured concurrency. File contents are read without a metadata-stripping step.

data_operations.operation: Upload encrypted manifest and wrapped root key
data_operations.source: Upload manifest construction, encryptManifest and wrapRootKey
data_operations.data_scope: Display name, creation time, file names/relative paths, inferred MIME types, original modification times, sizes, chunk parameters, nonces and metadataStripped flag. rootKey is encrypted under a key derived from linkKey.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured Xdrop API receives the encrypted manifest at /transfers/{transferId}/manifest and wrappedRootKey at /finalize. A subsequent downloader with the fragment key can recover the metadata.
data_operations.condition: After all file chunks complete. The plaintext manifest and unwrapped root key are not submitted by these calls.

data_operations.operation: Return the share capability to the caller
data_operations.data_scope: Share URL containing transferId and the linkKey fragment; JSON additionally contains transferId and expiresAt.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: stdout of the invoking process; no onward disclosure is shown.
data_operations.condition: After successful finalization, including quiet mode. Returning this capability is part of the declared sharing outcome.

data_operations.operation: Request deletion of an unsuccessful upload
data_operations.data_scope: Transfer identifier and manageToken; deletion targets the remote transfer.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured Xdrop API, DELETE /transfers/{transferId}. Actual erasure is outside the supplied source.
data_operations.condition: Only failures after entering the upload try block trigger cleanup. Rejected deletion requests are swallowed; successful transfers are retained for sharing. Earlier count/size failures bypass this block.

data_operations.operation: Parse the share capability locally and request public transfer metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Full share URL is read locally; transferId is sent to the API. The fragment key is decoded locally, while fragment and query are removed from the URL used to derive the server origin.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local memory holds linkKey. Configured download API receives GET /public/transfers/{transferId} and returns status, manifest location and wrappedRootKey.
data_operations.condition: A valid /t/:transferId link with a key fragment is required. Download stops unless the descriptor is ready and contains the required fields.

data_operations.operation: Fetch encrypted manifest/chunks and decrypt locally
data_operations.source: Download main, downloadFile and decryption helpers
data_operations.data_scope: API receives transferId and fileId/chunkIndex pairs. Descriptor.manifestUrl and returned chunk URLs are fetched; encrypted metadata and content are received, then decrypted using linkKey and rootKey.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured API receives the chunk-URL request. Hosts named by descriptor.manifestUrl and returned chunk URLs receive GET requests for those URLs. Plaintext metadata/content and unwrapped keys are processed locally.
data_operations.condition: For a ready transfer; every manifest file and chunk is downloaded. The code does not send the fragment key or unwrapped rootKey in these requests.

data_operations.operation: Persist decrypted files and return saved locations
data_operations.data_scope: Decrypted file contents and sanitized manifest relative paths; absolute output locations are collected for the result.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Chosen local output directory, defaulting to ./xdrop-{transferId}. Existing destination files are truncated by open(..., 'w'). stdout returns one saved path/output root, or JSON with transferId, outputRoot and all saved paths.
data_operations.condition: During download. Parent directories are created; finally closes the file handle but does not remove partial plaintext after failure. JSON/path output is explicitly documented.

data_operations.source: Upload/download logStatus calls and top-level error handlers
data_operations.data_scope: Upload server URL, transfer identifier, relative file paths, file counts and byte totals as applicable. Errors can include paths or messages returned by the API.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: stderr of the invoking process; any further capture or retention is not specified.
data_operations.condition: Progress is emitted unless --quiet is set. Errors are still emitted in quiet mode.

data_operations.data_scope: A small temporary file and its returned transfer link.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Xdrop upload destination, followed by a public transfer API request or opening the link in a browser.
data_operations.condition: Only if the user wants verification. This is an instruction to the agent, not an automatic verifier in the packaged scripts; browser behavior is unspecified.

potential_excess.data_scope: Original file modification times, extension-inferred MIME types, manifest creation time and basename duplicated alongside relativePath.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Encrypted manifest submitted to the configured API's /transfers/{transferId}/manifest; recoverable by a downloader possessing the share capability.
potential_excess.condition: Every manifest upload includes these fields, although the bundled downloader does not use them to reconstruct files.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Encrypted file transfer and preservation of relative paths require content and reconstruction metadata; these additional attributes are implementation choices. This is extra data within a required upload.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep an encrypted manifest sufficient to locate, decrypt and save the selected files.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Omit unused timestamps and inferred MIME metadata; omit name when a usable relativePath is present.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep fileId, usable relativePath/name, plaintextSize, chunkSize, totalChunks and noncePrefix. Preserve explicitly requested display names. Check compatibility with other intended Xdrop clients before changing the manifest format.

potential_excess.data_scope: Relative file paths in routine upload/download progress messages.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Invoking process stderr and any caller-managed capture.
potential_excess.condition: Default non-quiet execution emits paths repeatedly during transfers.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Progress reporting is optional implementation behavior. Successful transfer output is separately returned to stdout; path-bearing progress adds data to those diagnostic writes.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Transfer files and return the share link or saved-file result; optionally show useful progress.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use file indexes/counts and byte progress without paths, or select --quiet when diagnostic capture is unnecessary.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain required final results and useful failure diagnostics. Do not treat the intended share-link return or documented JSON file list as an unrelated disclosure.

potential_excess.data_scope: An unfinalized transfer record after early validation failure, or an unsuccessful transfer's uploaded ciphertext when cleanup fails.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured Xdrop API and its backing storage; actual retention is unknown.
potential_excess.condition: Creation succeeds but count/size validation fails before the try block, or a later DELETE request rejects and its error is swallowed.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Failed uploads need no continuing share artifact; the entry explicitly preserves transfer cleanup. This is potentially avoidable residual state, rather than extra fields in a successful upload.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Obtain server upload configuration, validate limits and clean up unsuccessful transfers.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Enter the cleanup-protected region immediately after creation, covering subsequent validation. Report unresolved deletion failures and use an appropriate bounded retry policy.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep successful transfers available for sharing. Creation may still be necessary to obtain server limits; do not assume a successful DELETE guarantees backend erasure.

potential_excess.data_scope: Incomplete decrypted file bytes left after a failed download.
potential_excess.condition: A chunk fetch, decryption or write fails after the destination is opened; finally closes the handle without removing the incomplete file.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Saving successfully decrypted files is required. Retaining unusable partial plaintext is an implementation consequence, not an explicit requirement.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Write complete decrypted files to sanitized intended destinations.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Write each file to a temporary destination, remove it on handled failure and promote it only after successful completion.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain completed requested files, preserve path sanitization, and avoid deleting a pre-existing destination during failure cleanup.

unknowns: Server and storage implementations are absent. Actual persistence, expiry enforcement, DELETE semantics, backups, request logging and access controls cannot be established.
Runtime API destinations and manifest/chunk URL hosts are unspecified; exact external organizations receiving requests cannot be identified.
The server's minimum registration-field requirements and other clients' manifest dependencies are absent. Removing plaintextBytes or unused manifest fields requires compatibility validation.
Optional browser verification behavior, including fragment-key handling and browser persistence, is outside the supplied source.
